issues.legal_issue: The corporate veil may be lifted where corporate entities and share transactions are used to conceal the effective sale or transfer of assets or to further a dishonest design.
material_facts: The allottee company’s parent transferred subsidiaries, including the Indian subsidiary, to another company, and the evidence described the sale of those subsidiaries and the transfer of their liabilities.
Affidavits also described a transaction involving a further investor and control over the relevant corporate assets.
The allottee withheld details of the transaction despite a direction to disclose them, and its account conflicted with statements in the affidavits placed before the Court.
issues.conclusion: The Court lifted the corporate veil and treated the evidence of the transactions as revealing their true character; the respondent had also suppressed material facts and violated the Court’s disclosure direction.
issues.legal_principle: Under Juggilal Kamlapat v. Commissioner of Income-tax, U.P., AIR 1969 SC 932; Jai Narain Parasrampuria (Dead) v. Pushpa Devi Saraf, (2006) 7 SCC 756; State of U.P. v. Renusagar Power Co., AIR 1988 SC 1737; and Life Insurance Corporation of India v. Escorts Ltd., AIR 1986 SC 1370, a court may lift the corporate veil when it is used to perpetrate fraud, evade tax, or further a dishonest or fraudulent design.

predicates.corporate_relationships_used_to_effect_t: Related corporate entities used their ownership or control relationships to carry out the transaction under examination.
predicates.evidence_showed_asset_or_subsidiary_sale: Evidence before the Court showed that corporate assets or subsidiaries had been sold or transferred.
predicates.material_transaction_details_withheld: A party withheld material details of the transaction despite a direction to disclose them.

issues.definition: When related corporate entities use their relationships to carry out a transaction and evidence shows an asset or subsidiary sale or material details are withheld, the corporate veil may be lifted.

issues.legal_issue: A restriction on transferring allotted property is breached when transactions formally described as share transfers effectively sell or transfer the property or its owning assets to another entity without permission.
material_facts: A site was allotted subject to a restriction on transfer for a specified period, and the allotment terms permitted substitution in certain corporate reorganizations only subject to stated conditions and permission.
The allottee’s shares and corporate assets were transferred through transactions involving another company, and the evidence indicated that the site was treated as part of the transferred assets.
The allottee had not obtained permission for the transactions and had not commenced construction before the allotment was cancelled.
The High Court had set aside the administrative orders resuming the site.
issues.conclusion: The transactions violated the transfer restriction, the resumption of the site was legal and proper, and the High Court’s order was set aside.
issues.legal_principle: Rule 9 of the Allotment of Small Campus Site in Chandigarh Information Services Park Rules, 2002, and clause 15 of the allotment letter restricted transfer of the site during the specified period. Clause 15 also provided limited circumstances for substitution following a merger, split, or subsidiary formation, subject to statutory requirements, regulatory permission, and recorded reasons. Applying the corporate-veil principles in Juggilal Kamlapat v. Commissioner of Income-tax, U.P., AIR 1969 SC 932; Jai Narain Parasrampuria (Dead) v. Pushpa Devi Saraf, (2006) 7 SCC 756; State of U.P. v. Renusagar Power Co., AIR 1988 SC 1737; and Life Insurance Corporation of India v. Escorts Ltd., AIR 1986 SC 1370, the Court examined the substance of the transactions rather than their formal description.

predicates.appeal_challenges_order_setting_aside_re: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a decision that set aside an order resuming allotted property.
predicates.effective_transfer_of_allotted_property: Transactions involving the allottee or related entities effectively transferred the allotted property or the assets through which it was held to another entity.
predicates.transfer_permission_not_obtained: The allottee did not obtain the permission required for the effective transfer.

issues.definition: In an appeal from a decision setting aside resumption, an effective transfer of allotted property without required permission means the resumption is legal and proper.
